acceptedAnswer.text: For a 50–60% win-rate strategy, 3–5 consecutive losses is normal and expected multiple times per year — over ~100 trades, the exact expected longest run is 4.6 at 60% win rate and 6.0 at 50%. Even 7 in a row over hundreds of trades is very common, and near-certain at a 50% win rate given enough trades. A streak is the system working as designed, not proof it stopped working.

mainEntity.name: How many losses in a row is normal in trading?

acceptedAnswer.text: Three damages. Financial: the drawdown compounds — 10 straight losses on a ₹2,00,000 account leave ~9.6% down at 1% risk per trade, ~40.1% down at 5%, and recovery is asymmetric (the hole needs +10.6% to +67% back to heal). Psychological: the gambler's fallacy and recency bias make a scheduled streak feel like proof of failure. Behavioral: frustration → size-up → revenge trading → abandonment → capitulation converts a normal blip into a permanent drawdown. Only the financial damage is inevitable; the other two are pre-committable choices.

mainEntity.name: How do losing streaks affect my trading account?

acceptedAnswer.text: Pre-commit the rule in calm and execute it in the storm: daily max loss of 2–3% of capital, weekly cap of ~5%, and a consecutive-loss circuit breaker — after 2–3 losses, halve position size; at a pre-set count (three is the common one), stop for the day. A rule written before loss #1 beats a decision made at loss #8.

mainEntity.name: Should I stop trading during a losing streak?

acceptedAnswer.text: Decrease — halve size after 2–3 consecutive losses, and never double down to 'win it back.' Another multi-loss run is always mathematically around the corner, and doubled size digs at doubled depth from an underwater balance. Rebuild confidence with live trades at reduced size, then graduate back up only after a run of well-executed trades.

mainEntity.name: Should I increase or decrease position size during a losing streak?

acceptedAnswer.text: Compare the live streak against your backtest's own worst streak and its conditions, not against your feelings. If your run of 7 sits inside a tested history containing runs of 9, nothing abnormal happened. If the live streak reaches ~1.5× the backtest's worst, or losses are bigger than any tested case, pause and diagnose using a variance-vs-broken-edge checklist covering conditions, magnitude, sample size, and overfitting tests.

mainEntity.name: Is my losing streak normal, or is my strategy broken?

acceptedAnswer.text: Because random results arrive in clusters — that is what randomness looks like. At a 45% win rate, 5-loss runs arrive with an average occurrence spacing of about 20 trades (exact mean wait from a fresh start: 41.9 trades; median: 30), and 8-loss runs about every 119 in spacing terms. Trade long enough and the streak is scheduled, not unlucky — a profitable edge and a losing streak are roommates, not contradictions.

mainEntity.name: Why do losing streaks cluster even for profitable strategies?

acceptedAnswer.text: Recovery is asymmetric: the deeper the hole, the faster the required recovery grows — −10% needs +11.1% back; −50% needs +100%. On a ₹2,00,000 account, 10 straight losses at 1% risk per trade need +10.6% back; at 5% risk they need +67%.

mainEntity.name: How long does it take to recover from a losing streak?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Under the independence model, each trade's odds are unchanged after 5–6 losses — the belief that a win is 'due' is the gambler's fallacy, an established cognitive bias. Real markets are not coin flips (volatility clusters, regimes shift), so independence is the first-order model, not gospel — but under any model, the market keeps no ledger of what it owes you.
